title: Finiteness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ ($X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$. If $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $f_i$ is finite for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 01ZO).

proof.text: Finiteness at the limit implies affineness. The two pullback-map presentations are related by pullback.congrHom (Over.w f₀) rfl; pullback hom-ext identifies the raw map with the source-isomorphism followed by Over.pullback.map. Cancel this source isomorphism in IsAffineHom and apply affineness descent to obtain k >= i₀ with affine f_k.

proof.text: Choose the finite subcover of the affine cover of Y₀. For every covering affine open V_b restrict the finite-limit hypothesis to its inverse image and apply the local affine-open descent lemma with the known affine stage k. This gives j_b >= k and finiteness of that restriction at every i >= j_b.

proof.text: The finite range of b ↦ j_b is bounded above in the directed preorder. Choose an upper bound i of it, then a common upper bound i′ of i and k. The chosen k supplies Nonempty I, so finite boundedness also applies to an empty cover. Thus i′ >= k >= i₀ and every covering restriction is finite at i′.
